drug_class: Topical ophthalmic local anesthetic (numbing eye drop)
purpose: Proparacaine is a numbing eye drop used by eye doctors and other healthcare providers to temporarily numb the surface of your eye. It is used before certain eye exams, procedures, or minor surgeries so you do not feel pain or discomfort. You might receive it before having your eye pressure checked or before a foreign object is removed from your eye.
how_it_works: Proparacaine works by temporarily blocking the nerve signals on the surface of your eye that send pain messages to your brain. Think of it like a short-acting 'off switch' for the nerves in your eye. The numbing effect starts very quickly, usually within 30 seconds, and wears off on its own in about 15 to 20 minutes.
common_side_effects: Right after the drops are put in, you may feel a brief mild stinging or burning sensation that goes away quickly. Your eye may also look slightly red or feel a little irritated for a short time. Temporary blurred vision can occur as well.
warnings: This medication is only meant to be used in a clinical setting by a healthcare professional — it should never be used at home or repeatedly on your own. Overuse can actually damage the surface of your eye. Because your eye will be numb after receiving this drop, avoid rubbing your eye until the feeling comes back completely, as you could accidentally injure it without realizing it. Tell your provider about any eye allergies or reactions you have had to anesthetics in the past.
typical_dosing: For most eye procedures, one or two drops are placed directly into the eye that needs to be numbed. Sometimes a second drop is given after about 5 minutes if a longer effect is needed. Dosing is always done by a healthcare provider in a clinical setting — this is not a medication you would dose yourself at home.
